title: Confidence Diameter for Normalized Treatment-Effect Variable Importance in Randomized Trials as Heterogeneity Vanishes
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound result subfield with paper-score ceiling 7.1 below the 7.4 field floor and found no bounded in-scope repair.
gap_reasons: paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
The exact multiplicative order remains open when T is of logarithmic size because the exponential constants are unmatched.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved matching known-shell and endpoint expected-diameter rates, a global-honesty obstruction, and a two-sided exponential transition bracket in the binary-sign Hölder model; the authoritative math review passed with no findings. It did not identify the exact multiplicative order in the critical logarithmic window, and the delivered model remained too narrow for the field floor. A future re-raise should solve that transition or broaden the statistical experiment, while adding the omitted Paillard et al. comparator to the positioning audit.
tldr: For a randomized binary trial, the shell-wide and endpoint expected confidence diameters for normalized treatment-effect importance have matching rates as total CATE energy vanishes. Global honesty through exact homogeneity has a real cost: in a window where known-shell endpoint-one intervals shrink, globally honest intervals retain constant diameter. Above the full-dimensional detection scale, a rho-tuned construction and a direct binary likelihood mixture give an exponential transition bracket and identify a logarithmic regime where global and known-shell endpoint-one rates match.
gap: The scaled TE-VIM is identified at positive variance, but fixed-law influence-function normality does not control confidence diameter uniformly as that variance approaches zero. Component-testing results do not directly answer normalized, shell-honest diameter questions.
fill: Establish matching binary-trial minimax expected-diameter rates on known shells, endpoint-specific rates, and a proved separation from confidence sets honest through the full null correspondence.
